newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila power firm to tap futures market.
newsitem.headline: Manila power firm to tap futures market.

text.p: State-run National Power Corp (Napocor) plans to sell surplus electricity in the spot market on a daily basis, company officials said on Sunday.
Napocor president Guido Alfredo Delgado said the firm hoped to expand their plans later to include trading surplus electricity in the futures market.
Napocor, the Philippines' main power producer, is entering into long-term sales contracts with customers, the biggest of which is the Manila Electric Co, the country's main power distributor.
Delgado said Napocor was processing a mechanism that would allow it to sell options for its projected excess capacity not covered by long-term sales contracts.
He said Napocor was targeting the entire range of bulk users, from utilities to rural electric cooperatives.
"Buying options will allow bulk users to purchase electricity at lower prices than the contracted capacity or even trade the options with other players," he told reporters.
